intended_object: The set of open Weyl chambers of a root system with a chosen base: the open chambers w·C°, where w runs over the Weyl group and C° = {x | ⟨αᵢ^∨, x⟩ > 0 for all simple roots αᵢ} is the open fundamental (dominant) chamber (Humphreys §10.3; Bourbaki Ch. V §3). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is `Set.range (openWeylChamber P b)`. Here `openWeylChamber P b w` is `w • openDominantChamber P b`, and `openDominantChamber` is `{x | ∀ i ∈ b.support, 0 < P.coroot' i x}`, the open cone cut out by the simple coroots. So the definition is the set of all Weyl translates of the open fundamental chamber. That is the standard definition (Humphreys, Bourbaki), and in the classical setting it agrees with "connected components of the complement of the reflecting hyperplanes". The library proves this agreement separately (`iUnion_openWeylChamber_eq_setOf_isRegularWeight`).

On generality: the definition works for any root pairing over a commutative ring with a linear order, which is at least as general as the textbook setting of real (or ordered-field) root systems. Mathlib has `RootPairing.Base` and Weyl groups but no notion of Weyl chamber, so nothing more general exists to cite.

Degenerate cases cause no problem. With no simple roots, the open chamber is all of M and there is a single chamber. If the open dominant chamber is empty (possible when 2 is not invertible, as the module docs note), the set is {∅}. This is a natural consequence of the definition, and the library handles it with an explicit nonemptiness hypothesis where it matters.
